blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Logistics & Supply Chain, applied ai & generative ai at dataq soft covers the full lifecycle of enterprise intelligence: strategy and value mapping, platform build-out, model adaptation, retrieval architectures, multimodal systems, and the governance fabric that keeps every model auditable. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise ai strategy & roadmapping, generative ai platform engineering, llm fine-tuning & model operations — delivered on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Demand and capacity planning stale
Volume forecasts lag promotion cycles and market shifts; capacity buys and network design inherit the error.
Visibility stitched from portals
Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Dispatch and exception work manual
Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower — Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping, Generative AI Platform Engineering, LLM Fine-Tuning & Model Operations, RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: Customs/security regimes (AEO, C-TPAT) obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping
Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.
Generative AI Platform Engineering
One governed platform, many GenAI products: retrieval, guardrails and cost control as shared services.
LLM Fine-Tuning & Model Operations
Own your models: tune, distill and operate LLMs with measurable quality, controlled cost and enforceable policy.
RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems
Answers with citations, not vibes: permission-aware retrieval over your regulated document estate.
ETA prediction
Traffic, weather and history-driven ETA models per lane and mode (promise accuracy up; penalties down)
Damage detection
Vision models at docks for load/damage verification with dispute evidence (claims cycle time down)
Detention and dwell time
Down 25-40% with yard/dock orchestration
Exception resolution time
Hours instead of days via agentic remediation
Cold-chain excursions
Intercepted in transit, not at claims

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: Customs/security regimes (AEO, C-TPAT) and Food safety (where cold chain). Temperature evidence and recall duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
